item.title: Depachika Food Halls — Guide
item.description: Depachika — the food halls in the basement (chika) floors of Japanese department stores (depaato) — are among the most dazzling and delicious places to eat and shop in Tokyo. Found beneath upscale stores in areas like Ginza, Shinjuku and Nihonbashi, these vast, gleaming halls are packed with hundreds of counters and vendors selling an astonishing array of beautifully presented food: exquisite Japanese and Western sweets and cakes, elegant bento boxes, sushi and sashimi, deli dishes, tempura, wagashi (traditional confections), imported delicacies, teas, sake and more, all displayed like jewellery.

item.title: Hirome Market: Kochi's Lively Food Hall — Guide
item.description: Hirome Market is the beating heart of Kochi’s food culture, a lively covered hall in the city centre packed with dozens of small stalls and communal tables where locals eat, drink and socialise from morning till late. The undisputed star is katsuo no tataki — bonito seared over a fierce straw fire until smoky outside and rare within, sliced thick and served with garlic, salt or citrus ponzu. Around it you’ll find sashimi, fried treats, dumplings, local sake and much more, bought from whichever stall tempts you and eaten together at shared tables in a warm, boisterous atmosphere.
